faq.a: Halos come from thin, high clouds like cirrus and cirrostratus, about 5 to 10 kilometres up, where it is cold enough for clouds to be made of ice crystals.
asks: What causes a ring around the Moon?
What clouds are made of ice?

faq.q: Why is a halo always the same size?
faq.a: The six-sided shape of ice crystals bends light by a minimum of about 22 degrees, and light piles up near that angle. So the common halo always has a radius of about 22 degrees.
asks: How big is a sun halo?

faq.q: How big does a halo look?
faq.a: Hold your hand out at arm's length with fingers spread: from thumb tip to little finger tip is roughly 20 to 22 degrees, about the radius of a halo.
asks: How can I measure a halo?
How far is the halo from the Sun?

faq.q: Does a ring around the Moon mean rain?
faq.a: Sometimes. The thin ice clouds that make halos often spread ahead of a warm front, which can bring rain a day or so later. So the old saying is partly true, but not always.
asks: Is a halo a sign of bad weather?
Ring around the Moon weather saying

faq.q: How is a halo different from a rainbow?
faq.a: A rainbow is made by raindrops with the Sun behind you. A halo is made by ice crystals and appears around the Sun or Moon, in front of you.
asks: Why is a halo a full circle?

facts: The common halo has a radius of about 22 degrees around the Sun or Moon.
Halos are made by six-sided ice crystals in high clouds such as cirrostratus.
